gawc.csv.edition: The World According to GaWC 2024 (GaWC, Loughborough University / KU Leuven; 175 advanced-producer-services firms across 785 cities; 335 cities classified). As of 2026-10-04 this is still the latest edition. GaWC news up to September 2026 lists no 2026 World Cities release. The only GaWC ranking released in 2026 is "Global Media Cities 2025" (Feb 2026), which is a different product.
gawc.csv.published_date: 2024-10 (Loughborough University press release "London and New York remain most connected cities in the world within a network of 335 cities", October 2024)
gawc.csv.coverage_notes:
All 335 classified cities are included: Alpha++ 2, Alpha+ 8, Alpha 17, Alpha- 22, Beta+ 20, Beta 23, Beta- 28, Gamma+ 20, Gamma 25, Gamma- 25, High Sufficiency 26, Sufficiency 119. These totals match the official press release: 335 cities in total, 49 alpha, 71 beta and 70 gamma, which leaves 145 at the two sufficiency levels. Within each tier, rows follow the order of the official GaWC page. No city was left out and none was inferred.

Cross-check: for every tier, the set of cities taken from the official GaWC page (listed in its own order) matched the Wikipedia 2024 tier list (alphabetical, with countries) exactly. Wikipedia also supplied each city's country.

Name normalisations (GaWC spelling -> CSV):
- Kiev -> Kyiv
- Bangalore -> Bengaluru
- Calcutta -> Kolkata
- Ulan Bator -> Ulaanbaatar
- Arhus -> Aarhus
- Hannover -> Hanover
- Nurnberg -> Nuremberg
- Macao -> Macau
- Atlanta (GA) -> Atlanta
- Valencia (Spain) -> Valencia
- Santa Cruz -> Santa Cruz de la Sierra
- Birmingham (UK) / Birmingham (AL) -> Birmingham with GBR / USA
- San Jose (CA) / San Jose (Costa Rica) -> San Jose with USA / CRI
- Diacritics removed (Sao Paulo, Bogota, Dusseldorf, Zurich, Malaga, Malmo, Wroclaw, Lodz, Krakow, Poznan, Liege, Urumqi, Queretaro, Izmir, Asuncion, Medellin, Ciudad Juarez, San Luis Potosi, Brasilia, Cordoba)

Two city names appear twice and are told apart by country_iso3: Birmingham (GBR Gamma, USA Sufficiency) and San Jose (USA Gamma, CRI Gamma). The city plus country_iso3 pair is unique.

Notable 2024 placements, confirmed by both sources: Moscow is Sufficiency, Kolkata is Sufficiency, and Osaka is Gamma.
gawc.csv.caveats:
How the data was obtained: the organisation's egress policy blocked direct access, for both curl and WebFetch, to gawc.lboro.ac.uk, en.wikipedia.org, lboro.ac.uk, Wikipedia mirrors and archive.org. I did not try to get around the block. The list was therefore taken from the WebSearch tool's indexed copies of the official GaWC World Cities 2024 page and the Wikipedia article: domain-restricted queries returned each tier's membership, not raw page downloads. The risk of a transcription error is reduced because two independent views agree:
1. The ordered GaWC page split into contiguous blocks that matched each Wikipedia tier set exactly.
2. The tier counts reproduced the press-release totals exactly (49 / 71 / 70 / 335).
Even so, nobody has looked at the raw HTML. Once gawc.lboro.ac.uk can be reached, it is worth a quick manual spot-check against https://gawc.lboro.ac.uk/gawc-worlds/the-world-according-to-gawc/world-cities-2024/.

Territory codes: three cities sit in territories that have no row in the visa dataset's Passport column. They are coded with their own ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 codes, in line with the HKG and MAC convention:
- George Town -> CYM (Cayman Islands)
- Hamilton -> BMU (Bermuda)
- San Juan -> PRI (Puerto Rico)
Remap them, for example PRI -> USA, if joins need to hit a passport row. Every other code is in the visa dataset (Hong Kong HKG, Macau MAC, Taipei/Taichung/Kaohsiung TWN).

Other notes:
- City names are plain English, but "Xi'an" keeps its apostrophe.
- "Newcastle" means Newcastle upon Tyne (GBR), "Cebu" is Cebu City (PHL), "Portland" and "Richmond" are the US cities, and "Luxembourg" is Luxembourg City.
- Not git-committed.

gfci.csv.edition: GFCI 40 (Global Financial Centres Index 40, Z/Yen Partners and China Development Institute). Report file GFCI_40_Report_2026.09.16_v1.2.pdf. It is the newest edition published on or before 2026-10-04 and replaces GFCI 39 (26 March 2026).
primary_sources: https://www.longfinance.net/media/documents/GFCI_40_Report_2026.09.16_v1.2.pdf (official report; the URL is known only from the search index because the proxy blocked fetching it)
gfci.csv.coverage_notes:
The file holds all 117 centres in the GFCI 40 main index, ranks 1 to 117 with no gaps. The search index summary of the report says 139 centres were researched and 117 are in the main index. Several press items agree on 117: Seoul Economic Daily, the Da Nang coverage and the Long Finance summary. The 22 researched centres that are not ranked are left out on purpose.

Ratings fall strictly with rank, so there are no ties. From rank 2 to rank 69, rating equals 759 minus rank (New York 761 is the exception). Below rank 69 the gaps vary. This pattern was checked against independent press figures: Seoul 752, Busan 737, Hong Kong 756, Astana 702, Ho Chi Minh City 692 and Riyadh 713.

The top 20 was cross-checked against press coverage: the Hong Kong government release, Seoul Economic Daily, CrowdfundInsider, Delano (Luxembourg), Swiss coverage of Zurich, Geneva and Lugano, DIFC and Abu Dhabi coverage, and US coverage of San Francisco at 11. The report summary itself says that Zurich replaced San Francisco in the top 10, and that Abu Dhabi, Beijing and Osaka replaced Paris, Amsterdam and Frankfurt in the top 20.

Regional and country totals agree with the file:
- 12 mainland Chinese centres.
- 12 Latin America and Caribbean centres, with Bermuda, Cayman Islands and Mexico City as the top three.
- Asia/Pacific holds 6 of the top 10.
- Africa: Kigali is third in Africa, after Casablanca and Mauritius.
- Eastern Europe and Central Asia: Astana, Cyprus and Warsaw are the top three.
- Middle East and Africa: Dubai, Abu Dhabi, Casablanca and Riyadh are the top four.

Naming:
- GFCI's "Minneapolis/St Paul" is written as "Minneapolis".
- "GIFT City-Gujarat" is written as "GIFT City" with IND.
- Labuan is MYS. Da Nang is VNM.
- Centres that are not cities keep the GFCI label: Luxembourg, Jersey, Mauritius, Malta, Bermuda, Isle of Man, Guernsey, Monaco, Cyprus, Bahrain, Cayman Islands, Gibraltar, Liechtenstein, British Virgin Islands, Panama, Bahamas and Barbados.

Territories use their own ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 codes: Jersey JEY, Guernsey GGY, Isle of Man IMN, Bermuda BMU, Cayman Islands CYM, Gibraltar GIB and British Virgin Islands VGB. These 7 codes do not appear in the Passport column of passport-index-tidy-iso3.csv. Every other code does.

Nothing is missing from the ranking.
gfci.csv.caveats:
IMPORTANT ABOUT SOURCING: the network blocked fetching. WebFetch and curl both got a 403 policy denial from the egress proxy for zyen.com, longfinance.net, cdi.org.cn, wikipedia, every news site tried, and the KIFC and Luxembourg for Finance mirrors. So the official PDF could NOT be opened directly. Every row comes from WebSearch answers, which are summaries the search tool writes from its index. That index includes the GFCI 40 PDF and press articles.

The summaries are sometimes wrong. Some answers mixed in rows from older editions or gave answers that contradicted others. Examples: Moscow 88/614, Rome 60, Munich 73, Calgary 72, Bangkok 100. Every one of these was thrown out. A row was kept only if all of these held:
(a) at least two separate queries agreed on rank and rating, or an independent press article confirmed it;
(b) it fitted the strictly decreasing rating sequence;
(c) it agreed with the regional and country totals.

Weaker rows, each confirmed only by a second query that already named the rank: Monaco 70/686, Tehran 112/603, Moscow 100/638 and St Petersburg 104/628. A contradictory answer for Moscow was thrown out. These four are the ones most worth checking against the PDF when it can be opened.

Ratings for Boston 18, Washington DC 19 and Osaka 20 come from repeated top-20 tables in the search summaries. Press confirmed only their ranks.

Recommendation: when the official PDF can be reached, check this file against Table 1 of GFCI_40_Report_2026.09.16_v1.2.pdf. The file is not git-committed.

This is the newest edition I could find that publicly ranks all 100 cities by international arrivals. The 2025 edition (Top 100 City Destinations Index 2025, Bangkok #1 with 30.3m) is not used, because its full arrivals list is not public (details in caveats).

https://www.visualcapitalist.com/the-100-most-popular-city-destinations/ (Visual Capitalist infographic of the 2019-edition data: all 100 ranks plus arrivals in millions to 2 decimals)
https://www.iol.co.za/travel/travel-news/revealed-top-100-city-destinations-for-2019-38525917 (IOL: full rank order 1-100 from the 2019 edition)

https://news.gtp.gr/2019/12/04/athens-gains-ground-moves-up-43rd-spot-euromonitor-cities-report/ (GTP: Athens #43, Heraklion #66, Rhodes #97, with Euromonitor 2019 forecasts used to back-check 2018 values)

tourism.csv.coverage_notes:
The file has all 100 ranks (1-100) of the 2019 edition's ranking by 2018 international arrivals. No city is missing and no ranks are skipped. Every ISO3 code appears in the Passport column of the visa dataset. The arrivals column falls monotonically from rank 1 to 100, and the 100 rows sum to 650.56m.

How the list was built:
- Rank order comes from IOL's full 1-100 list. Visual Capitalist and Eager Journeys agree with it.
- Arrivals are in millions, rounded to 2 decimals, the precision Visual Capitalist publishes. Each value was checked against Wikipedia's figures for the same cities, which are exact to the hundred.
- Four values follow Wikipedia's exact figure where the Visual Capitalist value (as read by the search tool) differs by 0.01 to 0.03:
  - Bangkok: 24.18 (24,177,500)
  - Munich: 4.07 (4,066,600)
  - Heraklion: 3.37 (3,371,800). This also matches GTP's 2019 forecast of 3,034,600 at -10%.
  - Athens: 5.73, from Visual Capitalist. This matches GTP's 2019 forecast of 6,301,300 at +10%. Wikipedia's 5,755,000 would put Athens above Cairo, which contradicts the ranks.

Values that come only from secondary sources, because Wikipedia's table is wrong for these cities:
- Los Angeles 7.50 (Visual Capitalist and WP Travel)
- Las Vegas 6.59 (Visual Capitalist and WP Travel)
- Cairo 5.75 (Visual Capitalist only). It sits between Berlin 5.96 and Athens 5.73, as its rank requires.
- Jerusalem 3.93 (Visual Capitalist and Globes)

Problems in Wikipedia's 2018 table, which I corrected to match Euromonitor's own order:
- It adds Palma de Mallorca (#15) and Naples (#63), which are not in Euromonitor's list.
- It leaves out Cairo (Euromonitor #42).
- It puts Jerusalem at #52 with a non-Euromonitor 4.8m figure.
- It swaps Los Angeles with Las Vegas, and Warsaw with Krakow.
- Its numbering ends with Bengaluru at #101.

City names were normalised to plain English:
- New York (Euromonitor: New York City)
- Cancun, Krakow and Mugla, without diacritics
- Frankfurt (Frankfurt am Main)
- Bengaluru (Bangalore)
- Penang (Penang Island)
- Cebu (Cebu City)
- Buenos Aires (Buenos Aires City)
- Saint Petersburg
- Marrakech
- Kolkata
- Hurghada
- Delhi, kept as Euromonitor names it. Note that gawc.csv uses "New Delhi".
tourism.csv.caveats:
1. The edition is not the requested one. The 2025 edition's full arrivals list is not publicly available. Euromonitor's 2025 press release and its media coverage (CNN, Bangkok Post, Travel Noire, Wikipedia, Grokipedia) give only the top 10 by arrivals: Bangkok 30.3, Hong Kong 23.2, London 22.7, Macau 20.4, Istanbul 19.7, Dubai 19.5, Mecca 18.7, Antalya 18.6, Paris 18.3, Kuala Lumpur 17.3. StatRanker publishes a "2025 top 100", but its ranks 11-100 are its own modelled estimates, so I did not use them. Since 2021 Euromonitor ranks the 100 cities by an attractiveness index, and has not published arrivals for all 100 in the 2021-2025 editions; I checked 2023, 2024 and 2025. That leaves the 2019 edition (2018 data) as the latest complete ranking by arrivals. The list is therefore about 7 years old and before COVID. For example, Hong Kong is #1 here, Bangkok is #1 in 2025, and Mecca and Antalya are much lower here than in 2025. I did not mix editions.

2. Year column. It holds 2018, the year the arrivals were measured, not 2019, the year in the edition's title. If you want the edition year instead, every row would change to 2019.

3. Sources were read indirectly. This session's network policy blocks Wikipedia, euromonitor.com, visualcapitalist.com, iol.co.za and the news sites, for both curl and WebFetch. I read those pages only through WebSearch's per-page summaries, and Wikipedia through a public GitHub CSV copy of its table. The summaries showed some numeric noise of 0.01 to 0.03 (see the Bangkok, Munich and Heraklion notes), so every value was cross-checked between at least two sources or against the rank order. I could not see the primary Euromonitor PDF myself. The values for Cairo (5.75), Los Angeles (7.50), Las Vegas (6.59) and Jerusalem (3.93) are 2-decimal figures from secondary sources only.

4. Ties at 2 decimals are separated by the rank column: Kuala Lumpur/Istanbul 13.43, Beijing/Saint Petersburg 4.00, Honolulu/Hurghada 2.74, Porto/Rhodes 2.34.

5. Country codes:
   - Jerusalem is coded ISR, following Euromonitor's country assignment. Its status is politically contested; PSE also exists in the visa dataset.
   - Hong Kong is HKG, Macau MAC and Taipei TWN, as instructed.

6. Nothing was committed to git. The new directory data/benchmarks/ already held an untracked gawc.csv.

cost.csv.edition: Mercer Cost of Living City Ranking 2024 (survey conducted March 2024, published June 2024; 226 cities; New York = base city, USD). Every search result I saw still names 2024 as Mercer's latest public city ranking. I found no 2025 or 2026 Mercer edition.
cost.csv.published_date: 2024-06 (Mercer press release 'Hong Kong remains most expensive city in the world for international employees', mid-June 2024)
primary_sources: https://www.mercer.com/insights/total-rewards/talent-mobility-insights/cost-of-living/ (official 2024 ranking page; blocked by the egress proxy, so not fetched directly)
https://www.mercer.com/en-us/about/newsroom/hong-kong-remains-most-expensive-city-in-the-world-for-international-employees/ (global press release, ranks 1-21 plus regional highlights)
https://www.thedailyjagran.com/... ('Islamabad cheapest in world') and https://atqnews.com/... (Lagos, Abuja)
cost.csv.coverage_notes:
The file has 103 of Mercer's 226 cities. All rows come from one source and edition (Mercer 2024), sorted by rank, with no duplicate ranks or cities. Every country_iso3 code was checked against the Passport column of passport-index-tidy-iso3.csv.

How the list was built: Mercer's full 226-row table is on mercer.com, but every WebFetch to it was blocked by the egress proxy. So were the WebFetches to every site that reproduces it (globallybased, placebrandobserver, CNN, Wikipedia, files.hawaii.gov, datawrapper and others). curl reaches only GitHub. I rebuilt the list from WebSearch summaries of Mercer's regional press releases and national news coverage, and the session's 200-search budget then ran out.

Top 50: 39 of 50 ranks are present. Missing ranks: 22, 26, 27, 28, 36, 39, 44, 45, 46, 48, 50.

Left out on purpose: one search returned Washington DC 22, Atlanta 27, Seattle 28, Houston 50, Minneapolis 59, Pittsburgh 62, Portland 65 and Detroit 81. That summary was built from 2023-dated pages (Hawaii Data Book 2023, a 2023 city-data thread, Mercer's 2023 US release), so I could not confirm the figures are the 2024 edition. They would fill ranks 22, 27, 28 and 50 if confirmed. The US is pinned at maximum value in the methodology, so leaving them out has little effect on scores.

Not found at all: Perth, Barcelona, Macau, San Juan, Monaco (Mercer may not cover it), Prague, Warsaw, Athens, Budapest, Istanbul, Moscow, Johannesburg, Cairo, Nairobi, Karachi, Dhaka, Colombo, Almaty, Baku, Tbilisi, Kyiv, Caracas, Kingston and most other mid- and lower-table cities (ranks 55-223 are sparse).

Cross-check against other sources: not done. The search budget ran out before I could search EIU or Julius Baer. From memory only, unverified and not to be cited: EIU Worldwide Cost of Living 2023 (Nov 2023) top 10 was Singapore and Zurich (joint 1st), Geneva and New York (joint 3rd), Hong Kong 5, Los Angeles 6, Paris 7, then Copenhagen, Tel Aviv and San Francisco (joint 8th). I could not confirm the EIU 2024 or 2025 editions or the Julius Baer 2025 top 10. Recalled Julius Baer leaders are Singapore, London, Hong Kong, Monaco and Zurich. Both lists overlap heavily with Mercer's top 10 (Hong Kong, Singapore, Zurich, Geneva, New York, London, Los Angeles).
cost.csv.caveats:
1) None of the ranks were read from Mercer's own table. Each was taken from search-engine summaries of pages that quote Mercer 2024, so a transcription error is possible. These ranks are backed by two or more searches or by a headline: Hong Kong to Los Angeles (top 10), Copenhagen 11, Dubai 15, Tel Aviv 16, Shanghai 23, Beijing 25, Seoul 32, Tokyo 49, Milan 57, Rome 67, Osaka 146, Doha 121, Kuwait City 119, Mumbai 136, Taipei 69 and Lisbon 100. These rest on a single summary: Brussels 37, Madrid 76, Shenzhen 34, Guangzhou 71, Helsinki 40, Vienna 24, Paris 29 and Amsterdam 30.
2) Bottom three: one summary gave Abuja 226, Lagos 225, Islamabad 224, with garbled year-on-year changes. I used Islamabad 226, Lagos 225, Abuja 224 instead. That order matches the Daily Jagran headline 'Islamabad cheapest in world' and the atqnews headline naming Lagos and Abuja as Africa's cheapest. It needs checking against Mercer's table.
3) Taipei: one summary gave 57, which is its 2023 rank. Taiwan News confirms 2024 = 69 ('fell 12 spots').
4) Mercer 2024 is the latest public edition I could find. If Mercer has since published a 2025 or 2026 city ranking that the search index did not show, this file is out of date.
5) Before relying on this file, re-check it against the official Mercer table in a session with mercer.com access (or a raised search budget). Filling the 11 missing top-50 ranks and the confirmed-2024 US cities would bring it close to complete for the top 100.
6) City names follow the requested plain-English form. N'Djamena keeps its apostrophe, and Kuwait City and Panama City are used for Mercer's 'Kuwait' and 'Panama'. No field contains a comma, so none needed quoting. Nothing was committed to git.

gawc.csv.remaining_concerns:
I made no edits to the file. I found no errors, and all 335 rows were checked.

How I checked: gawc.lboro.ac.uk and en.wikipedia.org are blocked by egress policy (403 for both WebFetch and curl). The WebSearch budget for this session was already used up (200/200). I did not try to get around the block. Instead I used two third-party copies of the official World Cities 2024 page found through GitHub code search:
- https://raw.githubusercontent.com/reubenwxw/Morph_visualiser/HEAD/workfile/WorldCities2024rankings_with_coords.csv (335 rows, in page order)
- https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BlackArsenic88/dashboards/HEAD/global_cities.csv (one column per tier)

Both copies keep GaWC's own spellings, such as Kiev, Calcutta, Ulan Bator, Arhus, "Atlanta (GA)", "Birmingham (AL)", "San José (Costa Rica)" and "George Town (Cayman Islands)". That suggests they were scraped verbatim from the official page. The two copies match each other exactly, tier by tier and in the same order. They may share one upstream scrape, so they are not fully independent of each other.

Compared with them, all 335 rows of gawc.csv have the same order and tier. Every name difference is one of the builder's documented normalisations:
- Kiev->Kyiv, Bangalore->Bengaluru, Calcutta->Kolkata, Ulan Bator->Ulaanbaatar, Arhus->Aarhus, Hannover->Hanover, Nurnberg->Nuremberg, Macao->Macau
- Qualifiers removed: "(GA)", "(UK)", "(AL)", "(CA)", "(Spain)", "(Cayman Islands)"
- St Louis->St. Louis, Santa Cruz->Santa Cruz de la Sierra, diacritics removed
- The source's "High sufficiency" became the required label "High Sufficiency"

Tier counts are 2/8/17/22/20/23/28/20/25/25/26/119, which gives 335 in total, with 49 alpha, 71 beta and 70 gamma.

Structural checks:
- No duplicate (city, country_iso3) pairs. Birmingham and San Jose each appear twice, once per country, which is correct.
- All tier labels are valid, and tiers are in order with no gaps.
- All names are ASCII, with no stray whitespace.
- HKG, MAC and TWN (Taipei, Taichung, Kaohsiung) are correct, and no Chinese territory is coded CHN by mistake.
- I checked every country code by eye against the city.

Ambiguous countries:
- **Hamilton (kept as BMU):** The GaWC page gives only "Hamilton". The reubenwxw copy places it in Hamilton, Ontario by its coordinates, and the Ivysauro/CNRT GaWC 2020 table labels it Canada. A TV Tropes "Major World Cities" page built on the GaWC 2018 tiers (archived at jwzimmer-zz/tv-tropes) lists "Hamilton, Bermuda" next to "Halifax, Canada". The builder says Wikipedia's 2024 list also gives Bermuda. I kept BMU, but if Hamilton is actually the Ontario city, the code should be CAN.
- **Cordoba (kept as ARG):** The reubenwxw coordinates and the Ivysauro table point to Spain. TV Tropes lists "Córdoba, Argentina", and Argentina is far more plausible because Zaragoza is not classified. If it is the Spanish city, the code should be ESP.
- **Santa Cruz (BOL) is confirmed:** the reubenwxw coordinates wrongly put it in California, which shows that copy's geocoding is unreliable.
- **Codes outside the visa dataset:** CYM (George Town), BMU (Hamilton) and PRI (San Juan) are correct ISO alpha-3 codes, but none of them appears in the Passport column. Remap them, for example PRI->USA, if a join needs to match a passport row.

Edition: I could not reach the GaWC site directly. The case that 2024 is the latest rests on four points:
- GitHub code search found nothing for "GaWC 2026", "GaWC 2025" or "world-cities-2026".
- The builder reports that GaWC news up to September 2026 shows no new World Cities release.
- I know of no newer edition up to my training cutoff.
- GaWC's release cadence (2016, 2018, 2020, 2024) does not point to an overdue edition.

Someone should still spot-check the live GaWC page once it can be reached.

gfci.csv.remaining_concerns:
I made no edits. I could not show any row to be wrong, but most rows could not be checked against a GFCI 40 source.

ACCESS LIMITS: Web search was used up (200 of 200). WebFetch and curl were blocked for zyen.com, longfinance.net, cdi.org.cn, info.gov.hk, Wikipedia and every news site I tried. Only GitHub was reachable. I used GitHub code search, raw.githubusercontent.com and git sparse clones of public news-archive repos as independent copies of press coverage.

CONFIRMED FROM INDEPENDENT SOURCES:
(1) Edition. GFCI 40 was published on 16 Sep 2026, launched in Busan and Shenzhen. Sources: kaopu-news-archive 2026-09-16; a Chinese foreign ministry briefing on 17 Sep, via the xchuan/quotes wallstreetcn archive. GFCI comes out every March and September, so nothing newer can exist before 2026-10-04.
(2) Count. The index has 117 centres.
(3) Top 10 and top-4 ratings. HKEJ article 4515137 of 2026-09-16 gives the top 10 order: New York, London, Hong Kong, Singapore, Shanghai, Tokyo, Seoul, Shenzhen, Dubai, Zurich. It says London is 4 points behind New York, Hong Kong and Singapore are 1 and 2 points behind London, and Hong Kong scores 756. That gives 761, 757, 756 and 755, which all match the file. Source: Henrywzh/equity-research article backups.
(4) Seoul is 7th. Source: LeoHeo/ai-news, citing NewDaily on 2026-09-18.
